source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate simple (historical Ulmaceae family character), ovate or lanceolate blades 3–9 cm, entire or few-toothed; cuneate to cordate bases, obtuse to acuminate apex; 3 basal major veins (Celtis genus)
morphology_documented.flowers: Small; both staminate and perfect flowers present, calyces deeply lobed
morphology_documented.fruit: Small round smooth drupes in orange, brown, dull/dark red or reddish-black; pedicels equal or exceed subtending petioles; fruits persist beyond leaf fall

source_scope_note: Genus-level traits are expressly indicated; absent species details not inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: 1999 flora places Celtis in Ulmaceae; current repository assigns Cannabaceae
Flora treats laevigata, reticulata and texana as varieties of C. laevigata but discusses varietal boundaries as uncertain; do not assume all traits apply to all segregates
preservation: Additive record; original species.json, photos, credits and galleries unchanged
